inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: H1 FY2026 interim note 8 diluted weighted average 1,605,686,797 (basic 1,604,295,955 net of share-award trust + 1,390,842 unvested awards); issued shares 1,604,556,486. Held FLAT -- SBC (~US$3m/yr) is expensed in the flows and there is no non-SBC issuance.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report consolidated cash flow statement, 'Equity-settled share-based payments' US$3,014k (Annual_FY2025.txt:4068). Shares for the award scheme are bought on market (US$3.7m FY2025) rather than net-share settled, so there are no equity-award withholding taxes (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every year).
inputs.fx_note: Statements are in US$'000 (USD reporting); HKEX quote is HKD. All flows and per-share values computed in USD, converted at USD/HKD 7.8472 (Yahoo USDHKD=X, regular close 2026-10-10T21:00Z). Parity check: the HKD is pegged in the 7.75-7.85 convertibility band, and 7.8472 sits inside it, so the direction (HKD per USD, multiply) is confirmed; no USD dual listing to tie against. Unsuffixed intrinsic values are HKD; *_usd twins carry the model currency.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 for a cyclical contract manufacturer with China consumer retail attached, +0.8pp for operating-country exposure (Vietnam, Indonesia, China, India) -> cost of equity ~10%. Gearing is light (bank debt ~US$1.0bn against a ~US$2.7bn market cap, floating USD rate ~4.5-5% pre-tax), giving WACC ~9.5%. Same WACC in every scenario: cyclicality, tariff and customer-concentration risk are charged in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Reported EBITDA (US$779.1m FY2025 = operating profit ex interest income + D&A incl. right-of-use depreciation) is post-IFRS 16, so the full lease cash payment -- 'Repayment of lease liabilities, including related interests' US$102.7m FY2025 (1.28% of revenue), US$48.7m H1 FY2026 -- is deducted via lease_cost_pct_path at 1.25%. D&A path is EX right-of-use depreciation (PPE 262.4 + intangibles 2.0 = 264.4 = 3.29% of FY2025 revenue). Lease liabilities (US$194.9m at 30-Jun-2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt. Net debt is bank borrowings only, as the company itself defines it ('debt excludes lease liabilities').
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated, so NCI is deducted ONCE in the bridge. Pou Sheng International (3813.HK) is 62.55% owned; the 37.45% NCI is taken at MARKET value (5,315.5m shares x HK$0.37 at 2026-10-09 = HK$1,967m = US$250.6m; 37.45% = US$93.9m) rather than its US$454.9m book value, because Pou Sheng trades at ~0.2x book and its profit (US$29.3m FY2025, NCI share US$11.0m) does not support book. Individually immaterial NCI taken at book, US$40.0m (US$39.4m at Dec-2025). Total NCI deduction US$133.9m.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (USD-built WACC, HKD quote via fx_rate, lease treatment B, NCI in bridge, near-zero SBC, associates and financial assets in the bridge). Routing: Yue Yuen is an operating company -- the world's largest athletic footwear OEM (~70% of revenue) plus the consolidated China sportswear retailer Pou Sheng (~30%) -- so the operating-company/cyclical row of dcf-methods applies; no prior DCF or memory entry existed (fresh build). ANCHOR CHOICE: FY2025 revenue (US$8,031m) is the compounding base, but the forward margin is NOT FY2025's. H1 FY2026 EBITDA was ~US$285m (7.2% margin; derived as operating profit 112.0 less interest income 12.2 plus D&A 185.4) against ~US$374m (9.2%) in H1 FY2025; manufacturing gross margin fell to 14.3% from 17.7% on tariff-cost sharing with brand customers, labour-cost inflation and uneven production leveling, and management's H2 outlook says visibility has not improved. Year 1 (FY2026) therefore assumes ~7.8% EBITDA margin (H2 modestly better than H1, no full recovery). MID-CYCLE JUDGMENT: the base case recovers only to 9.0% by FY2029, about 1.2pp BELOW the FY2022-25 average of ~10.2%, because tariff-sharing and wage inflation look structural rather than one-off -- the brands are pushing cost onto OEMs and the India/Indonesia ramp adds start-up drag. Bull returns to 10.5% (FY2024 was 11.0%); bear stays ~7.5-7.7%. CAPEX: FY2025 total capex US$327m (4.1% incl. right-of-use and intangibles) and H1 FY2026 US$131m are elevated by the Central Java plant and the ~US$276m Tamil Nadu project; FY2021-24 ran 2.1-2.6%. Path glides 3.8% -> 3.1% against D&A ex-ROU 3.3% -> 2.9%. WORKING CAPITAL: manufacturer/retailer with receivables + inventory well above payables (net operating working capital ~22% of revenue), so wc_capture is NEGATIVE (-20%): growth consumes cash. CASH TAX: FY2025 taxes paid US$100.7m = ~24.6% of modelled EBIT; FY2025 book tax was flattered by a US$20.4m reversal of the Tax Disputes provision (FY2024 included a US$28.2m charge for it), so neither year's book rate is used -- 23% cash rate on operating EBIT (Pillar Two QDMTTs in Vietnam/Indonesia keep it from falling). Calibration: FY2025 modelled EBIT ~US$409m x 0.77 = 315 NOPAT + associates/JV 70 + after-tax interest/other ~29 - after-tax bank interest ~35 - NCI 14 = ~365 vs reported attributable US$381m -- ties within non-operating noise. INTEREST INCOME: not stripped from last_fcf because the group is in NET DEBT at 30-Jun-2026 (US$224.3m) and was only US$62.5m net cash at Dec-2025, far below 1x the FCF base; in any case EBITDA as built excludes interest income, so the forward flows contain none. SBC: ~0.04% of revenue -- effectively an SBC-zero market; row kept explicit, house and street bases nearly coincide so band_position is not meaningful. BUYBACKS: US$3.7m FY2025 is share-award-scheme purchases, not a capital-return programme; the flat count is a modelling convention, not funded by repurchases. YEAR-1 TIMING: FY2026 is ~78% elapsed at the valuation date but is discounted a full period under the house end-of-year convention; this slightly understates value. DIVIDEND: HK$1.30/share (~US$266m/yr) exceeds the base-case FY2026-27 owner FCF -- the 70% payout policy will either be cut or funded from the balance sheet if margins do not recover.

equity_bridge.item: Interests in associates and joint ventures at book
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 balance sheet: associates US$447.4m + JVs US$145.9m (HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:336-337). Share of results (US$69.9m FY2025; US$25.3m H1 FY2026) is excluded from EBITDA, so the asset is added here; book is ~8.5x FY2025 share of profit and ~US$68.5m/yr of cash dividends, so book is not generous.

H1 FY2026: FVTPL non-current US$143.7m + current US$43.8m + other financial assets at amortized cost US$51.8m (HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:340-355). Their returns are outside EBITDA; the H1 FY2026 jump was funded from cash (US$128m acquired), so excluding them would make the net-debt rise look like value destruction.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests (Pou Sheng 37.45% at market + other NCI at book)
equity_bridge.note: See inputs.nci_treatment. Pou Sheng 3813.HK HK$0.37 x 5,315.5m shares x 37.45% / 7.8472 = US$93.9m; other NCI US$40.0m.
H1 FY2026 balance sheet US$83.7m (HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:400); debt-like, defined-benefit cost (US$13.9m FY2025) is a non-cash add-back in OCF so it is not otherwise charged.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (3.3-3.5%) diverges by more than 30% from revenue CAGR (-3.6% 3yr, -1.0% 5yr) and EPS 3yr CAGR (+8.8%, off a weak FY2022 base). Book growth reflects retained earnings, not top-line growth; the forward revenue path (base -1% FY2026, 2-3% thereafter) is built from shipment volume x ASP, not from book CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs end FY2025. EPS 5yr CAGR undefined (FY2020 EPS was a loss of US$0.056). Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (equity-award taxes zero; interest income not stripped as the group is not materially net cash): FY2020 578.5, FY2022 699.5, FY2025 271.7 -- the steep negative CAGRs are driven by working-capital releases in FY2020/FY2022-23 and the FY2025 capex step-up, not by SBC (SBC is ~US$3-5m/yr, so the SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs are effectively identical). Reported FCF also does not deduct ~US$100-200m/yr of lease payments.

base.narrative: Tariff-sharing becomes a permanent ~1pp drag; FY2026 trough ~7.8% EBITDA margin, partial recovery to 9.0% by FY2029 as India/Indonesia capacity levels production and labour is re-aligned; revenue flat-to-low-single-digit growth on ASP and modest volume share gains from China-exit sourcing.

bull.narrative: Tariff regime settles and brands re-normalise ordering; Yue Yuen wins share as Nike/Adidas/New Balance consolidate China-exit volume with the most diversified OEM; ASP premiumisation continues; Pou Sheng stabilises on digital/livestream. Margin returns to ~10.5% (FY2024 was 11.0%).

bear.narrative: H1 FY2026 conditions persist: brands keep pushing tariff and wage cost onto OEMs, volume is reallocated toward Vietnamese/Indonesian peers and the parent's own capacity, India ramps slowly into under-utilisation, and Pou Sheng keeps shrinking as Anta/Li Ning go direct. Margin stuck ~7.5%.

scenario_narratives.base: Yue Yuen's two axes are OEM manufacturing margin (tariff-cost sharing with Nike/Adidas, wage inflation in Vietnam/Indonesia/China, production leveling as capacity shifts to Indonesia and India) and the slow erosion of Pou Sheng's China distribution model. The base case treats the 2026 margin compression as partly structural: H1 FY2026's 7.2% EBITDA margin is a trough, but the recovery stops at 9.0%, ~1.2pp below the FY2022-25 average, because brands have shown they can push tariff cost onto suppliers and will keep doing so. Revenue grows 2-3% a year on ASP and modest share gains from China-exit sourcing while Pou Sheng shrinks; capex normalises after the India build.
scenario_narratives.bull: Tariffs settle into a predictable regime and the 2026 cautious-ordering cycle reverses (as the 2023 destock did into 2024). The largest, most geographically diversified OEM takes share as brands consolidate their supplier base away from China; ASP premiumisation (+3.7% in FY2025) continues; Indonesia and India reach efficient utilisation; Pou Sheng stabilises on digital channels. EBITDA margin returns to 10.5%, close to the FY2024 peak of 11.0%, and revenue compounds 4-5% for several years.
scenario_narratives.bear: The H1 FY2026 margin is the new normal. Customer concentration bites: Nike and Adidas keep reallocating volume and sharing tariff cost, India's new capacity ramps into weak demand, wage inflation outruns ASP, and Pou Sheng keeps closing stores (-200 net in H1 FY2026) as domestic brands disintermediate it. Revenue falls in FY2026-27 and grows ~1.5% thereafter; margin stays ~7.5%; the 70% payout is cut.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: earnings are actively deteriorating (H1 FY2026 attributable profit -58%), management flags no inflection, and the business depends on two customers who have demonstrated they can push tariff cost onto suppliers. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things -- a settled tariff regime, a brand reorder cycle, efficient India ramp and a stable Pou Sheng -- to go right together. Base at 50% as the central partial-recovery path.
probability_weighted.weights_rationale_bear: Structural tariff-sharing plus customer concentration with no flagged inflection.
probability_weighted.weights_rationale_base: Partial margin recovery to below the prior-cycle average is the most likely path.
probability_weighted.weights_rationale_bull: Requires tariff, reorder, India-ramp and Pou Sheng recoveries simultaneously.
probability_weighted.band_note: Band collapsed: SBC is ~0.04% of revenue (US$3m/yr), so house and street differ by ~HK$0.2/share and the price sits far outside the degenerate band; band_position is not meaningful and is set null (SBC-zero market convention).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Yue Yuen as a cyclical contract manufacturer on a deliberately below-prior-cycle mid-cycle margin, with leases charged in the flows, the associates and financial-asset portfolio added at book, and Pou Sheng's minority taken at market. The question is not whether FY2025 recurs but how much of the 2026 tariff-sharing squeeze is permanent; the base case assumes most of it.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin recovery: every 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly HK$4-5/share; the base already sits below the FY2022-25 average.
Customer concentration: Nike and Adidas order reallocation can move volume by double digits in a year.
Tariff policy: US tariffs on Vietnam/Indonesia/China-made footwear and how much brands push back onto OEMs.
Capex overrun or slow ramp in India (~US$276m) and Indonesia.
Dividend: the HK$1.30 payout (~US$266m) exceeds near-term owner FCF; holding it raises net debt.
Bridge items at book (associates/JVs US$593m, financial assets US$239m) are ~30% of equity value; a haircut to them moves the answer materially.
